title: Resilient burn-rate backoff and contextual pager suppression
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: After a capacity regression incident on dedicated pools we observed sharp, short-lived burn-rate spikes that caused cascading pager noise across multiple oncall rotations. This ticket defines changes to make burn-rate alerting and paging more resilient to transient capacity fluctuations while preserving fast detection of real SLO degradations.
problem_statement: Current burn-rate alerts trigger immediate paging on short bursts (1–3 minute spikes) that are typically remediated by autoscaler or fallback routing. These spurious pages increase oncall fatigue and delay focus on sustained degradations. We need an approach that: (1) avoids paging for transient spikes under a configurable tolerance window, (2) keeps early awareness for escalating persistent breaches, and (3) scopes noise reduction to non-customer-critical routes so we don't mask real customer-impacting outages.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume from burn-rate alerts reduced by >=60% for non-critical routes during transient capacity events (measured over 14-day windows)
No increase in undetected sustained SLO breaches: sensitivity test shows >=95% detection of multi-minute outages simulated in chaos runs
New alert config is live in prod and documented in Console runbook
Oncall runbook updated with escalation flow and manual override instructions
proposed_changes: Introduce an adaptive burn-rate smoothing layer (EMA with tunable alpha per route tier) that mutes single-minute spikes from immediate pagering
Add a configurable minimal burn exposure window (default 3 minutes) before triggering P0 paging; shorter visibility-level alerts (Slack/console) are still emitted at 1 minute
Implement per-customer aggregation key to deduplicate simultaneous signals caused by a single upstream event
Add hysteresis/backoff to paging: first page at sustained breach, subsequent pages only if breach persists past backoff interval or severity escalates
Label routes by criticality (critical | important | best-effort) so suppression rules don't apply to critical customer-impacting routes
implementation_plan: Design ETA & config schema in alerting service (Lucas) — 2 days
Runtime change: add smoothing/aggregation primitives to burn-rate pipeline (Nina & Rahul) — 3 days
Console/UI: expose tier labels and backoff config (Riley) — 2 days
Staging rollout: enable for non-critical routes, run synthetic chaos + canary dashboards (team) — 3 days
Gradual prod rollout with monitoring and kill-switch feature flag — 2 days
Post-rollout observation window and tuning session with oncall rotation — 7 days
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged rollout with immediate kill-switch. If we observe missed sustained breaches (detection <95% in canary tests) revert smoothing at the feature-flag gate and re-evaluate parameters. Pagering can be re-enabled to previous config within 15 minutes via the kill-switch.
test_plan: Unit tests for EMA smoothing and aggregation key behavior
Integration tests: simulate short (1–3m) spikes and verify no paging but console alert exists
Chaos test: simulate autoscaler lag + capacity regression and verify progressive alerting escalation
Replay historical incident traces (Jan–Feb capacity events) to measure false-positive reduction
Oncall tabletop exercise to validate runbook and manual override
